# `jarvis-client` — every source file, in one document

Commit `a0ec449885add309e6fdd7f0b4d972483b622635` on `studio-chat-fixes-3`.

Generated by `tools/gen_source_bundle.py`, not written by hand. The previous
version of this file was hand-written and went stale without saying so — it
described this module as "step 0, no networking" long after it had grown a
network layer, an audio stack and a voice loop.

Contains the whole `jarvis-client` module, plus the CI workflows that build it,
because how a thing is tested is part of judging whether it works.

**423 files included.**

Deliberately omitted, listed so their absence is visible rather than silent:

- `jarvis-client/app/src/main/res/mipmap-hdpi/ic_launcher_foreground.png` — binary image
- `jarvis-client/app/src/main/res/mipmap-hdpi/ic_launcher_monochrome.png` — binary image

## `.github/workflows/android-apk.yml`

````yaml
name: Build Android APK

# Builds jarvis-android, and only jarvis-android.
#
# This used to be a generic detector that worked out whether the repo held a
# Gradle, Flutter, React Native or Capacitor project. That was right when the
# repo might contain any of them; it is wrong now that it holds two Gradle roots,
# because the detector picked one with `find … | head -n1` — readdir order, not a
# choice. It returned jarvis-client in a local checkout and jarvis-android on the
# runner, so which app the "epic-jarvis-debug-apk" artifact contained was decided
# by the filesystem. The path filter below says what this workflow is for; the
# working directory now says the same thing.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      java_version:
        description: "JDK version used for the Gradle build"
        default: "17"
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
    # The desktop endpoint has no bearing on the APK.
    # keystore/ is in here because the build now reads the shared debug key from
    # it. Rotating that key changes what every APK is signed with, and without
    # this the change would build nothing.
    paths:
      - "jarvis-android/**"
      - "keystore/**"
      - ".github/workflows/android-apk.yml"

# Read only: this workflow no longer publishes a release (see the end of the
# file), so nothing here writes to the repository.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: android-apk-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PROJECT_DIR: jarvis-android

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - name: Put the signing key back
        # From the DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64 repository secret, not from the repo. The
        # key used to be committed; it was public, so it was removed and
        # replaced. build.gradle.kts still reads keystore/debug.keystore from
        # the repository root, so that is where this writes it.
        #
        # github.workspace is explicit because jarvis-client.yml sets a
        # job-level working-directory of jarvis-client, and this file does not
        # belong there.
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        env:
          KEY: ${{ secrets.DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::The DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64 secret is missing. Stopping on purpose:"
            echo "::error::build.gradle.kts guards the keystore on exists(), so the build"
            echo "::error::would NOT fail - it would sign with a throwaway key, and"
            echo "::error::adb install -r over the copy on the phone would then fail with"
            echo "::error::INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, forcing an uninstall that"
            echo "::error::wipes the pairing secret."
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p keystore
          printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64 -d > keystore/debug.keystore
          echo "Signing key restored."


      - uses: actions/setup-java@dded0888837ed1f317902acf8a20df0ad188d165 # v5.0.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ inputs.java_version || '17' }}
          cache: gradle

      - uses: android-actions/setup-android@be39fa834029ff78f1a44aa3bb0819b8fc2bd8fd # v4.0.4
        with:
          # Not the default `tools platform-tools`. Google removed the obsolete
          # `tools` package from the SDK repository, so the action's own default
          # makes it run `sdkmanager tools`, get "Failed to find package 'tools'",
          # and fail the job before a line of this project is compiled. Nothing
          # here ever used it; platform-tools is the half that is real.
          packages: platform-tools

      # Unit tests gate the APK. The assertion on the results directory is the
      # point: `testDebugUnitTest` reports NO-SOURCE and exits 0 when it is
      # pointed at a module with no test sources, so a green check here used to
      # be compatible with nothing having run at all.
      - name: Run unit tests
        working-directory: ${{ env.PROJECT_DIR }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          set -o pipefail
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          if ! ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --stacktrace 2>&1 | tee test.log; then
            echo "::group::Kotlin errors"
            grep -E "^e: |Unresolved reference|Argument type mismatch|None of the following candidates|Compilation error" test.log | head -80 \
              || echo "(no compiler diagnostics found; see the full log above)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi
          results=app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest
          if ! ls "$results"/TEST-*.xml >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::No test results in $results — the test task matched no sources."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Test classes executed:"
          ls -1 "$results"/TEST-*.xml
          # Belt and braces: a results file can exist with zero tests in it.
          total=$(grep -ho 'tests="[0-9]*"' "$results"/TEST-*.xml \
                  | grep -o '[0-9]*' | paste -sd+ - | bc)
          echo "Total tests: ${total:-0}"
          if [ "${total:-0}" -lt 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::Test results contain zero tests."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Upload test reports
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6.0.0
        with:
          name: jarvis-android-test-reports
          path: ${{ env.PROJECT_DIR }}/app/build/reports/tests/**
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

      # Debug only. The app is sideloaded over adb and never listed, so there is
      # no distribution channel a release build would serve — and the keystore
      # plumbing that used to live here fed four SIGNING_* variables into a build
      # that contained no signingConfig to read them, producing an unsigned APK
      # that cannot be installed while CI and the README both called it signed.
      - name: Build debug APK
        working-directory: ${{ env.PROJECT_DIR }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          set -o pipefail
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          if ! ./gradlew assembleDebug --stacktrace 2>&1 | tee build.log; then
            echo "::group::Kotlin errors"
            grep -E "^e: |^w: .*error|Unresolved reference|Compilation error" build.log | head -80 \
              || echo "(no compiler diagnostics found; see the full log above)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Collect APK
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p artifacts
          found=0
          while IFS= read -r apk; do
            cp "$apk" artifacts/
            echo "Found $apk"
            found=1
          done < <(find "$PROJECT_DIR" -name '*.apk' -print)
          if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::The build reported success but produced no .apk file."
            exit 1
          fi
          ls -lh artifacts

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6.0.0
        with:
          name: jarvis-android-debug-apk
          path: artifacts/*.apk
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

      # This workflow no longer publishes a release, and the reason is not
      # tidiness. `android-latest` sat next to `client-latest` with a nearly
      # identical name, and only one of them can talk to the backend:
      # jarvis-android speaks a WebSocket protocol invented before
      # JARVIS-API.md existed, and none of its endpoints are implemented
      # server-side. Two similar links where one silently cannot work is a trap
      # rather than a choice, and installing the wrong one reads as "my phone is
      # broken" rather than "wrong app".
      #
      # The module itself stays, and so does the build above. Its duplex audio,
      # lock-screen approvals and Glance widgets are worth porting into the real
      # client, and a module that still compiles is a much easier thing to port
      # from than one that rotted quietly. The run artifact is still produced
      # for anyone who actually wants this APK.
````

## `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

````yaml
# The 21 unit tests in this repo had nothing to run them until now, and the
# checks below are exactly the ones that were being typed by hand — including
# the two that would have caught real bugs: `cargo test` covers the ported
# colour engine, the SSE frame parser and the process-tree killer, and the
# markdown suite covers a parser that ran on every streamed token.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
    # A push that changes ONLY these files runs nothing: no test reads them
    # (checked 2026-09-26 - the suites read docs/*.md, backend/README.md and
    # CHANGELOG.md, so those are NOT listed). Every changed file must be on
    # this list for a run to be skipped; one other file and everything runs.
    paths-ignore:
      - "CLAUDE.md"
      - "README.md"
  # Pull requests into main only (every other branch is already checked by
  # its push). No path filter here, so a required check on a pull request
  # always reports instead of waiting for a run that never starts.
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# A newer push to the same branch (or pull request) stops the older run: its
# result would be out of date before it finished.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Nothing here writes to the repository.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Every action is pinned to a full commit, like the other workflows (a tag can
# be moved to different code after it was checked). The tag each commit stood
# for on 2026-09-26, read from that action's own tag list, is beside it. All
# of them run on Node 24 (Node 20 is being retired on GitHub's runners).

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  rust:
    # The product is a Windows app. Checking it anywhere else would type-check
    # the wrong half of every `#[cfg(windows)]`.
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: jarvis-desktop/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      # Pinned to a commit, this action cannot read the toolchain from its
      # ref, so it is named here (as in desktop-release.yml).
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@6bed0761d98439e5a578e2877258200ad565ba87 # stable branch
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          workspaces: jarvis-desktop/src-tauri
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test

  frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: jarvis-desktop
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      # No bundler and no test framework: the pages are plain ES modules, so a
      # parse check is what there is. It would have caught nothing in this
      # repo's history — the frontend bugs were behavioural — but it is the
      # floor, and the markdown suite below is the part that matters.
      - run: for f in src/*.js; do node --check "$f"; done
        shell: bash
      - run: node scripts/markdown-test.mjs
      - run: python3 scripts/check-tokens.py
      # EVERY suite in tests/, not a hand-picked few. Most of them open the
      # real pages in a headless Chromium (tests/uikit.mjs), which is why only
      # three used to run here. Playwright is not a dependency of the app
      # (tests/README.md says why), so it is installed for this job only.
      # uikit.mjs is the harness, not a suite; shots.mjs only writes
      # screenshots. Every suite runs even after one fails, so one red run
      # lists every failure at once.
      - name: Install Playwright's Chromium (for the page tests only)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund playwright
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Every desktop test suite
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          failed=()
          for f in tests/*.mjs; do
            name=$(basename "$f")
            case "$name" in uikit.mjs|shots.mjs) continue ;; esac
            echo "::group::$name"
            if node "$f"; then echo "ok  $name"; else failed+=("$name"); fi
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          if [ "${#failed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::${#failed[@]} desktop suite(s) failed: ${failed[*]}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Every desktop suite passed."

  backend:
    # The backend suites, including every contract test (the ones that read
    # the phone's Kotlin and the desktop's Rust and JS and check them against
    # the real Python). About twenty suites test a patch against the owner's
    # own jarvis_hud.py / jarvis_gate.py / jarvis_extract.py, which are not in
    # this repository - backend/run_suites.py SKIPS those by name, with the
    # files each is waiting for, and fails on anything else. The voice suites
    # (test_speech, test_voice_contract, test_wakeword) need the three voice
    # packages from backend/requirements.txt, and test_chat_log needs
    # `cryptography` (chat history is encrypted); nothing else from it is needed,
    # and the memory ones (fastembed, sqlite-vec) are left out on purpose -
    # the suites use a hash embedder and must pass without them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
        with:
          # The WHOLE history, not the last commit: test_patch_history.py
          # rebuilds backend/patch-history from `git log` and fails if the
          # committed copy differs. In a shallow clone it has nothing to
          # read, and with CI set it fails rather than skip.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@e797f83bcb11b83ae66e0230d6156d7c80228e7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check numpy sherpa-onnx onnxruntime cryptography
      - name: Backend suites (the ones that need no file from the owner's PC)
        run: python backend/run_suites.py
      # Desktop and phone call the same backend; a route one calls and the
      # other does not has to be a recorded decision (tools/check_parity.py).
      - name: Desktop / phone parity
        run: python tools/check_parity.py
      # The animal faces' shader is generated for both apps from one source
      # (tools/gen_critters.py), and must stay under the size Android's shader
      # compiler accepts: over it, Android refuses the shader and the phone
      # app crashes the moment the face is drawn - while the desktop, and a
      # newer Skia on a PC, accept it without a word. The first red panda
      # shipped four times over and was caught only by the emulator test.
      - name: Animal faces - generated copies fresh, shader within Android's size limit
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y -q glslang-tools > /dev/null
          python tools/gen_critters.py --check
          python tools/shader_size.py --check
      # The mouths' lip-sync analysis is written twice - lipsync.js on the
      # desktop, LipSync.kt on the phone - and the phone's LipSyncTest checks
      # its copy against a fixture the JavaScript writes. A stale fixture
      # would let the two drift apart with every test still green.
      - name: Lip-sync - the phone's golden fixture matches lipsync.js
        run: python tools/gen_lipsync.py --check
      # A command registered in lib.rs but missing from build.rs's own ACL
      # export list has no permission at all, and every window's call to it
      # is refused at runtime - a compile-time-invisible break that bit two
      # commands for real (bug audit 2026-09-27, desktop-rust finding #2).
      - name: Desktop command ACL parity
        run: python tools/check_command_acl.py

  credential-manager:
    # The pairing token lives in Windows Credential Manager (CLAUDE.md rule 3,
    # backend/jarvis_token_store.py). Linux has no Credential Manager, so the
    # backend job above only tests the logic against a stand-in; this runs the
    # real ctypes calls - write, read back, move an old file in, delete - on
    # real Windows, under a throwaway name, never a real token. The same for
    # the four account secrets (ease-of-use audit row 15) that reuse the same
    # store through jarvis_token_store.resolve_secret.
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@e797f83bcb11b83ae66e0230d6156d7c80228e7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Token store, live against Credential Manager
        run: python backend/test_token_store.py
      - name: Account secrets, live against Credential Manager
        run: python backend/test_account_secrets.py

  powershell-5:
    # The owner runs these scripts in Windows PowerShell 5.1, not 7. 5.1 does
    # not know `??`, `?:`, `&&` or `||`, and reads a script file that has no
    # BOM as ANSI (Windows-1252), not UTF-8 - so a non-ASCII character in
    # code can become a quote mark and end a string early. Caught here, by
    # 5.1 itself, before the owner has to paste an error back. Then
    # apply-patches.ps1 is actually RUN, in 5.1, against a stand-in backend,
    # to prove it copies what it ships and never overwrites a settings file.
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: powershell
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - name: Parse every .ps1 with Windows PowerShell 5.1
        run: |
          "PowerShell $($PSVersionTable.PSVersion)"
          if ($PSVersionTable.PSVersion.Major -ne 5) { throw "expected Windows PowerShell 5.x" }
          $bad = 0
          $files = @(Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File -Filter *.ps1 | Where-Object { $_.FullName -notmatch '\\node_modules\\' })
          foreach ($f in $files) {
            # Get-Content with no -Encoding reads the way 5.1 reads a
            # script: ANSI, unless the file starts with a BOM.
            $text = Get-Content -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Raw
            $tokens = $null; $errors = $null
            [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput($text, [ref]$tokens, [ref]$errors)
            foreach ($e in $errors) {
              $bad++
              "::error file=$($f.FullName),line=$($e.Extent.StartLineNumber)::$($e.Message)"
            }
            foreach ($t in $tokens) {
              if ($t.Kind -ne 'Comment' -and $t.Text -match '[^\x00-\x7F]') {
                $bad++
                "::error file=$($f.FullName),line=$($t.Extent.StartLineNumber)::non-ASCII outside a comment ($($t.Kind)); 5.1 reads this file as ANSI"
              }
            }
            "parsed  $($f.FullName)"
          }
          "$($files.Count) script(s), $bad problem(s)"
          if ($bad -gt 0) { exit 1 }
      - name: Run apply-patches.ps1 in 5.1 against a stand-in backend
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          # A copy of the repository's scripts and backend with the patch
          # list emptied: the stand-in has no real jarvis_hud.py for a patch
          # to apply to. What is under test is everything after patching:
          # the modules, the backups, the settings file.
          $repo = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'repo'
          $be = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'backend'
          $cfg = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'cfg'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $repo, $be, $cfg | Out-Null
          Copy-Item -Recurse scripts, backend -Destination $repo
          Remove-Item (Join-Path $repo 'backend\*.patch')
          $ps1 = Join-Path $repo 'scripts\apply-patches.ps1'
          $t = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($ps1)
          $t2 = [regex]::Replace($t, '(?s)\$PATCHES = @\(.*?\n\)', '$$PATCHES = @()')
          if ($t2 -eq $t) { throw "could not empty the patch list" }
          [IO.File]::WriteAllText($ps1, $t2)
          Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $be 'jarvis_hud.py') -Value 'print("stand-in")'
          Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $be 'jarvis_notes.py') -Value '# an older copy'
          $env:OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR = $cfg

          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ps1 -BackendPath $be -SkipPackages -SkipTests
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "first run exited $LASTEXITCODE" }

          # Every shipped module is there, and is this repository's copy.
          $where = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $repo 'backend\_where.py'))
          # Only the SHIPPED tuple: the rest of _where.py names other files too
          # (HUD = BACKEND / "jarvis_hud.py"), and one of those is the owner's own.
          $block = [regex]::Match($where, '(?s)\nSHIPPED = \((.*?)\n\)').Groups[1].Value
          $shipped = @([regex]::Matches($block, '"((?:rebuilt/)?jarvis_\w+\.py)"') | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value })
          if ($shipped.Count -lt 20) { throw "read only $($shipped.Count) names from _where.SHIPPED" }
          foreach ($m in $shipped) {
            $leaf = Split-Path -Leaf $m
            $got = Join-Path $be $leaf
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $got)) { throw "$leaf was not copied in" }
            $want = Join-Path (Join-Path $repo 'backend') $m
            if ((Get-FileHash $got).Hash -ne (Get-FileHash $want).Hash) { throw "$leaf is not the repository's copy" }
          }
          "all $($shipped.Count) shipped modules were copied in"
          $backups = @(Get-ChildItem -Directory -LiteralPath $be -Filter '_jarvis-backup-*')
          if ($backups.Count -eq 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $backups[0].FullName 'jarvis_notes.py'))) { throw "the older jarvis_notes.py was not backed up" }
          "the older jarvis_notes.py was backed up"

          # There was no settings file anywhere, so one went beside jarvis_hud.py.
          $toml = Join-Path $be 'jarvis-framework.toml'
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $toml)) { throw "no jarvis-framework.toml was installed" }

          # The owner edits it; a second run must leave it exactly as it is.
          Add-Content -LiteralPath $toml -Value "`n[ci_owner_edit]`nkept = true"
          $before = (Get-FileHash $toml).Hash
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ps1 -BackendPath $be -SkipPackages -SkipTests
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "second run exited $LASTEXITCODE" }
          if ((Get-FileHash $toml).Hash -ne $before) { throw "the second run changed the owner's jarvis-framework.toml" }
          "the owner's settings file was left alone"
      - name: apply-patches.ps1 in 5.1 replaces an OLDER version of a patch
        run: |
          # The owner may have run the script before some patches were edited
          # here, and the current text of an edited patch cannot take its old
          # text off. So: a made-up backend and a made-up list of three
          # patches. The backend carries the first patch and an OLD text of
          # the second (the third was added to the list since). The script
          # must find that old text in backend\patch-history - after trying a
          # newer old text that is NOT there - take it off, and leave exactly
          # what the current list gives. A text that was never published
          # must be refused with the file untouched and no backup made.
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          # Native programs run with 'Continue', so what they write to
          # stderr is output, not a terminating error (CLAUDE.md's trap).
          function Invoke-Native([string] $Exe, [string[]] $Arguments) {
            $prev = $ErrorActionPreference
            $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
            try { $out = & $Exe @Arguments 2>&1 | Out-String; $code = $LASTEXITCODE } finally { $ErrorActionPreference = $prev }
            return @{ Code = $code; Out = $out }
          }
          function Assert-Native([string] $Exe, [string[]] $Arguments) {
            $r = Invoke-Native $Exe $Arguments
            if ($r.Code -ne 0) { throw "$Exe $($Arguments -join ' ') exited $($r.Code): $($r.Out)" }
          }
          function Write-Lf([string] $Path, [string] $Content) {
            [IO.File]::WriteAllText($Path, $Content, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
          }
          # Why two texts differ, in one line: a wrong LINE ENDING (Windows
          # git turning LF into CRLF on write) reads very differently from
          # wrong CONTENT, and the first time this step ran on Windows it
          # failed without saying which.
          function Get-Diff([string] $Got, [string] $Want) {
            $cr = ([regex]::Matches($Got, "`r")).Count
            $same = ($Got -replace "`r`n", "`n") -eq $Want
            return "got $($Got.Length) chars with $cr CR; expected $($Want.Length) chars with 0 CR; same apart from line endings: $same"
          }
          function Assert-Text([string] $Path, [string] $Want, [string] $Why) {
            $got = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($Path)
            if ($got -ne $Want) { throw "$Why - $(Get-Diff $got $Want)" }
          }
          # What the SCRIPT leaves. Windows git with its default
          # core.autocrlf=true reads a file as LF and writes it back CRLF -
          # measured here on 2026-09-24: all 40 lines came back CRLF, the
          # content otherwise identical. Python reads both the same, and git
          # reads it back as LF again, so a second run still recognises every
          # patch (case 2 checks exactly that). So the content must match
          # exactly, and the endings must be ONE kind throughout - a file
          # with some CRLF lines and some LF lines is refused.
          function Assert-Result([string] $Path, [string] $Want, [string] $Why) {
            $got = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($Path)
            $cr = ([regex]::Matches($got, "`r`n")).Count
            $lf = ([regex]::Matches($got, "`n")).Count
            if (($got -replace "`r`n", "`n") -ne $Want) { throw "$Why - $(Get-Diff $got $Want)" }
            if ($cr -ne 0 -and $cr -ne $lf) { throw "$Why - mixed line endings: $cr of $lf lines are CRLF" }
            return $got
          }
          # A 40-line jarvis_hud.py with some lines changed (0-based index).
          function Get-Hud([hashtable] $Changes) {
            $lines = @(1..40 | ForEach-Object { "line $_" })
            foreach ($k in $Changes.Keys) { $lines[$k] = $Changes[$k] }
            return (($lines -join "`n") + "`n")
          }
          # A git-format patch taking jarvis_hud.py from one state to another.
          function New-ToyPatch([hashtable] $Before, [hashtable] $After, [string] $Out) {
            $g = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'toy-gen'
            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $g) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $g -Recurse -Force }
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $g | Out-Null
            Assert-Native 'git' @('-C', $g, 'init', '-q')
            Assert-Native 'git' @('-C', $g, 'config', 'core.autocrlf', 'false')
            Write-Lf (Join-Path $g 'jarvis_hud.py') (Get-Hud $Before)
            Assert-Native 'git' @('-C', $g, 'add', 'jarvis_hud.py')
            Write-Lf (Join-Path $g 'jarvis_hud.py') (Get-Hud $After)
            Assert-Native 'git' @('-C', $g, 'diff', "--output=$Out")
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Out) -or (Get-Item -LiteralPath $Out).Length -eq 0) { throw "no patch written to $Out" }
          }

          $one    = @{ 4 = 'line 5 - one' }
          $twoOld = @{ 4 = 'line 5 - one'; 19 = 'line 20 - two, as first published' }
          $decoy  = @{ 4 = 'line 5 - one'; 19 = 'line 20 - two, some other old text' }
          $never  = @{ 4 = 'line 5 - one'; 19 = 'line 20 - two, hand-edited, never published' }
          $twoNew = @{ 4 = 'line 5 - one'; 19 = 'line 20 - two, as it is now'; 24 = 'line 25 - two, added later' }
          $three  = @{ 4 = 'line 5 - one'; 19 = 'line 20 - two, as it is now'; 24 = 'line 25 - two, added later'; 34 = 'line 35 - three' }

          # A copy of the repository with the made-up list and history.
          $repo = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'repo-old'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $repo | Out-Null
          Copy-Item -Recurse scripts, backend -Destination $repo
          $pd = Join-Path $repo 'backend'
          Remove-Item (Join-Path $pd '*.patch')
          Remove-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $pd 'patch-history') -Recurse -Force
          New-ToyPatch @{} $one (Join-Path $pd 'toy-one.patch')
          New-ToyPatch $one $twoNew (Join-Path $pd 'toy-two.patch')
          New-ToyPatch $twoNew $three (Join-Path $pd 'toy-three.patch')
          $hist = Join-Path $pd 'patch-history\toy-two'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $hist | Out-Null
          New-ToyPatch $one $decoy (Join-Path $hist 'bbbbbbb.patch')
          New-ToyPatch $one $twoOld (Join-Path $hist 'aaaaaaa.patch')
          $tab = [char]9
          Write-Lf (Join-Path $pd 'patch-history\index.tsv') (
            "# made up for this test`n" +
            "toy-two.patch${tab}toy-two/bbbbbbb.patch${tab}bbbbbbb0000${tab}2026-09-02T00:00:00+00:00${tab}an old text that is not on the backend`n" +
            "toy-two.patch${tab}toy-two/aaaaaaa.patch${tab}aaaaaaa0000${tab}2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00${tab}the old text the backend has`n")
          $ps1 = Join-Path $repo 'scripts\apply-patches.ps1'
          $t = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($ps1)
          $t2 = [regex]::Replace($t, '(?s)\$PATCHES = @\(.*?\n\)', '$$PATCHES = @(''toy-one.patch'', ''toy-two.patch'', ''toy-three.patch'')')
          if ($t2 -eq $t) { throw "could not replace the patch list" }
          [IO.File]::WriteAllText($ps1, $t2)
          $cfg = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'cfg-old'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $cfg | Out-Null
          $env:OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR = $cfg
          $runArgs = @('-NoProfile', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-File', $ps1, '-SkipPackages', '-SkipTests', '-BackendPath')

          # 1. The first patch and the OLD second one are on: replaced.
          $be = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'backend-old'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $be | Out-Null
          $hud = Join-Path $be 'jarvis_hud.py'
          Write-Lf $hud (Get-Hud @{})
          # autocrlf off for THIS setup only, so the stand-in is exactly what
          # an LF backend holds. The script's own git calls are left alone:
          # if Windows git changes endings under them, the checks below
          # must see it.
          Assert-Native 'git' @('-c', 'core.autocrlf=false', '-C', $be, 'apply', (Join-Path $pd 'toy-one.patch'))
          Assert-Native 'git' @('-c', 'core.autocrlf=false', '-C', $be, 'apply', (Join-Path $hist 'aaaaaaa.patch'))
          Assert-Text $hud (Get-Hud $twoOld) "the stand-in backend was not built as intended"
          $r = Invoke-Native 'powershell' ($runArgs + @($be))
          $r.Out
          if ($r.Code -ne 0) { throw "the run on a backend with an older patch exited $($r.Code)" }
          $after = Assert-Result $hud (Get-Hud $three) "the result is not what the current list gives"
          if ($r.Out -notmatch 'OLDER version') { throw "it did not say it found an older version" }
          if ($r.Out -notmatch 'toy-two\.patch from 2026-09-01 \(commit aaaaaaa\)') { throw "it did not name the older version it found" }
          $bk = @(Get-ChildItem -Directory -LiteralPath $be -Filter '_jarvis-backup-*')
          if ($bk.Count -ne 1) { throw "expected one backup folder, found $($bk.Count)" }
          Assert-Text (Join-Path $bk[0].FullName 'jarvis_hud.py') (Get-Hud $twoOld) "the backup is not the file as it was before the run"
          "an older toy-two.patch was recognised, taken off and replaced; the backup holds the file as it was"

          # 2. Run again: everything is on, nothing changes.
          $r = Invoke-Native 'powershell' ($runArgs + @($be))
          if ($r.Code -ne 0) { throw "the second run exited $($r.Code)`n$($r.Out)" }
          if ($r.Out -notmatch 'already applied') { throw "the second run did not find everything applied`n$($r.Out)" }
          # Byte for byte: a second run must not touch the file at all.
          Assert-Text $hud $after "the second run changed the file"
          "a second run found everything applied"

          # 3. A text of the second patch that was never published: refused,
          #    nothing changed, no backup.
          $be2 = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'backend-never'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $be2 | Out-Null
          $hud2 = Join-Path $be2 'jarvis_hud.py'
          Write-Lf $hud2 (Get-Hud $never)
          $r = Invoke-Native 'powershell' ($runArgs + @($be2))
          $r.Out
          if ($r.Code -eq 0) { throw "a never-published text was not refused" }
          if ($r.Out -notmatch 'NOTHING HAS BEEN CHANGED') { throw "the refusal did not say nothing was changed" }
          Assert-Text $hud2 (Get-Hud $never) "the refused run changed the file"
          if (@(Get-ChildItem -Directory -LiteralPath $be2 -Filter '_jarvis-backup-*').Count -ne 0) { throw "the refused run made a backup folder, so it got past the rehearsal" }
          "a never-published text was refused and nothing was touched"

          # 4. Nothing on yet: the whole current list goes on.
          $be3 = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'backend-fresh'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $be3 | Out-Null
          $hud3 = Join-Path $be3 'jarvis_hud.py'
          Write-Lf $hud3 (Get-Hud @{})
          $r = Invoke-Native 'powershell' ($runArgs + @($be3))
          if ($r.Code -ne 0) { throw "the run on a fresh backend exited $($r.Code)`n$($r.Out)" }
          [void](Assert-Result $hud3 (Get-Hud $three) "a fresh backend did not get the current list")
          "a fresh backend got the whole current list"
          # Explicitly: the runner ends a powershell step with the LAST native
          # exit code, and case 3 above expects one that is not 0.
          exit 0

  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: jarvis-desktop/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@6bed0761d98439e5a578e2877258200ad565ba87 # stable branch
        with:
          toolchain: stable
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@9983c65e42da123ff25d1f78505eb6de315aa172 # v2.87.20
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny
      - run: cargo deny check licenses advisories
      # THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt must name every Rust library the Windows
      # build ships, with its copyright lines (DEPS audit B-22). After adding
      # or updating a crate: python3 tools/gen_notices.py, and commit the file.
      - name: Third-party notices are up to date
        run: |
          cargo fetch --locked
          python3 ../../tools/gen_notices.py --check

  python-advisories:
    # The backend's Python packages, next to `cargo deny` above (feasibility
    # audit I111, first half, 2026-09-26): backend/requirements.lock must pin
    # every package in requirements.txt with a hash, and no pinned release -
    # on any platform or Python version the lock covers - may have a known
    # advisory in PyPI's own database. Standard library only, so there is
    # nothing new to install (or to pin) for the check itself.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@e797f83bcb11b83ae66e0230d6156d7c80228e7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Python packages are hash-locked and have no known advisory
        run: python tools/check_python_advisories.py
````

## `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`

````yaml
# Builds the Windows installer for Jarvis Desktop and, once the owner has
# added a signing key, publishes it where the app looks for updates.
#
# What it needs from the owner, once (jarvis-desktop/README.md, "Turning on
# updates", has the exact steps):
#
#   * the PUBLIC key in jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json
#     (plugins.updater.pubkey) - it goes into the app, so the app can check
#     every download;
#   * the PRIVATE key and its password as repository secrets
#     TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY and TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD.
#
# Until both are there it still builds, unsigned, and keeps the installer as
# a run artifact - but it publishes nothing and fails nothing. An update the
# app cannot verify is worse than no update, so there is no unsigned path to
# the release.
#
# Which branches publish: main and the owner's working branch
# `claude/admiring-ritchie-5urg5h` only (the owner installs from those, like
# the phone). Since 2026-09-26 no other branch starts this workflow on a push
# (other claude/ branches used to, and whichever pushed last replaced the
# owner's download). "Run workflow" by hand still builds any branch, keeping
# the installer as a run artifact only. The release notes and latest.json name
# the branch and commit, so a build from the working branch is never mistaken
# for one from main.
#
# Where it publishes: the rolling release tagged `desktop-latest`, the exact
# URL in tauri.conf.json. Not `/releases/latest/`: that is whichever full
# release in the whole repository is newest, which says nothing about the
# desktop, and the phone's `client-latest` lives in the same repository.
#
# The version: tauri.conf.json's major.minor (the shared VERSION file at the
# top of the repository, 0.2.0 since 2026-09-26) plus this workflow's run
# number (0.2.<n>), so every published build is newer than the last and newer
# than the 0.2.0 a hand-built copy reports. The updater only offers a HIGHER
# version, so a rolling build that kept 0.1.0 would never be offered.
name: Desktop release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    # main, and the owner's working branch (the owner installs from those,
    # as with the phone's client-latest).
    branches: [main, "claude/admiring-ritchie-5urg5h"]
    paths:
      - "jarvis-desktop/**"
      - ".github/workflows/desktop-release.yml"

# Read only by default; the one job below, which publishes, may write.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: desktop-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  TAG: desktop-latest

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: write
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: jarvis-desktop
    # Every action is pinned to a full commit, as the Android workflows are
    # (apps security audit L7): this job handles the updater's signing key,
    # and a tag can be moved to different code after it was checked. The tag
    # each commit stood for on 2026-09-25 is in the comment beside it, read
    # from that repository's tag list (2026-09-26 for checkout, setup-node and
    # upload-artifact, moved off Node 20). To update one, look up the new
    # tag's commit the same way and change both.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      # Pinned to a commit, this action cannot read the toolchain from its
      # ref any more (it used to be `@stable`), so it is named here.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@6bed0761d98439e5a578e2877258200ad565ba87 # stable branch
        with:
          toolchain: stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          workspaces: jarvis-desktop/src-tauri

      # Decides three things up front, and says why, so a run that publishes
      # nothing is a clear notice rather than a mystery.
      - name: Decide what this run can do
        id: plan
        env:
          # A yes/no only. The key itself is not read here.
          HAS_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY != '' }}
          IS_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) }}
          IS_WORK_BRANCH: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/claude/admiring-ritchie-5urg5h' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pubkey=$(node -e 'const c = require("./src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"); const k = ((c.plugins || {}).updater || {}).pubkey || ""; process.stdout.write(k.trim() ? "yes" : "no")')
          base=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(String(require("./src-tauri/tauri.conf.json").version || ""))')
          if ! [[ "$base" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tauri.conf.json has version '$base', not major.minor.patch."
            exit 1
          fi
          version="${base%.*}.${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}"

          sign=false
          publish=false
          if [ "$HAS_KEY" != "true" ]; then
            why="The TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret is not set, so this build is unsigned and nothing is published. See jarvis-desktop/README.md, 'Turning on updates'."
          elif [ "$pubkey" != "yes" ]; then
            why="The signing secret is set, but tauri.conf.json has no public key (plugins.updater.pubkey), so the app could not check a signed download. Nothing is signed or published until it is added."
          else
            sign=true
            if [ "$IS_DEFAULT_BRANCH" = "true" ] || [ "$IS_WORK_BRANCH" = "true" ]; then
              publish=true
              why="Signed, and published to the '$TAG' release as version $version, from $GITHUB_REF_NAME."
            else
              why="Signed, but $GITHUB_REF_NAME is neither main nor the owner's working branch, so it is not published."
            fi
          fi

          echo "::notice::$why"
          {
            echo "### Jarvis Desktop $version"
            echo ""
            echo "$why"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          {
            echo "version=$version"
            echo "sign=$sign"
            echo "publish=$publish"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # `npm ci`, from the committed package-lock.json: exactly the versions
      # (and checksums) in the lockfile, or the step fails. `npm install`
      # with the `^2.1.0` range took whatever was newest on the day.
      - name: Install the Tauri command-line tool
        run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund

      # The committed config has createUpdaterArtifacts off, so a build on
      # the owner's PC works with no key. It is switched on here, and only
      # when this run can sign; the version is stamped the same way. Merged
      # from a file, which Tauri accepts in place of inline JSON and which
      # survives Windows argument quoting untouched.
      - name: Build the installer
        env:
          KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          SIGN: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.sign }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          here=$(pwd -W 2>/dev/null || pwd)
          conf="$here/release.conf.json"
          printf '{"version": "%s", "bundle": {"createUpdaterArtifacts": %s}}\n' "$VERSION" "$SIGN" > "$conf"
          cat "$conf"
          if [ "$SIGN" = "true" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$KEY_PASSWORD"
          fi
          unset KEY KEY_PASSWORD
          npx tauri build --config "$conf"

      # Renamed to names with no spaces, so the download URL is the plain
      # file name. A signature covers the file's bytes, not its name.
      - name: Collect the installers
        env:
          SIGN: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.sign }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          bundle=src-tauri/target/release/bundle
          nsis=$(find "$bundle/nsis" -maxdepth 1 -name '*-setup.exe' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
          msi=$(find "$bundle/msi" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.msi' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
          if [ -z "$nsis" ]; then
            echo "::error::No NSIS installer was built under $bundle/nsis."
            exit 1
          fi
          nsis_out="dist/jarvis-desktop_${VERSION}_x64-setup.exe"
          msi_out="dist/jarvis-desktop_${VERSION}_x64_en-US.msi"
          cp "$nsis" "$nsis_out"
          if [ -n "$msi" ]; then cp "$msi" "$msi_out"; fi
          if [ "$SIGN" = "true" ]; then
            if [ ! -f "$nsis.sig" ]; then
              echo "::error::The build was asked to sign but wrote no $nsis.sig."
              exit 1
            fi
            cp "$nsis.sig" "$nsis_out.sig"
            if [ -n "$msi" ] && [ -f "$msi.sig" ]; then cp "$msi.sig" "$msi_out.sig"; fi
          fi
          ls -l dist

      - name: Keep the installer with this run
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6.0.0
        with:
          name: jarvis-desktop-${{ steps.plan.outputs.version }}
          path: jarvis-desktop/dist/*
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Write latest.json
        if: steps.plan.outputs.publish == 'true'
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          msi="dist/jarvis-desktop_${VERSION}_x64_en-US.msi"
          msi_args=()
          if [ -f "$msi" ] && [ -f "$msi.sig" ]; then msi_args=(--msi "$msi"); fi
          node scripts/updater-manifest.mjs \
            --version "$VERSION" \
            --base-url "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/download/${TAG}" \
            --nsis "dist/jarvis-desktop_${VERSION}_x64-setup.exe" \
            ${msi_args[@]+"${msi_args[@]}"} \
            --notes "Jarvis Desktop ${VERSION}, built from commit ${GITHUB_SHA::7} on ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}. Install it from Settings -> Updates; nothing installs on its own." \
            --out dist/latest.json
          cat dist/latest.json

      # Rolling, like the phone's client-latest: the old release is removed
      # and this one takes its tag. For the few seconds in between, a check
      # from the app reads "no releases published yet" and tries again later.
      - name: Publish to the desktop-latest release
        id: publish
        if: steps.plan.outputs.publish == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          short="${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
          notes=$(printf '%s\n' \
            "Jarvis Desktop **$VERSION**, from commit \`$short\` on \`$GITHUB_REF_NAME\`." \
            "" \
            "Already installed and signed? Settings -> Updates -> Check now, then Install. Jarvis never installs an update on its own." \
            "" \
            "First time, or your copy says updates are not set up: download \`jarvis-desktop_${VERSION}_x64-setup.exe\` below and run it once." \
            "" \
            "Every installer here is signed; the app refuses a download whose signature does not match the key it was built with. This tag is rolling.")
          gh release delete "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --cleanup-tag --yes 2>/dev/null || true
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/* \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --target "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --title "Jarvis Desktop - latest ($VERSION)" \
            --notes "$notes" \
            --latest=false
          echo "Published: $(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json url --jq .url)"

      - name: Explain a failed publish
        if: failure() && steps.publish.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          echo "::warning::Could not publish the release. If the log above says 403," \
               "open the repository's Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow" \
               "permissions and choose 'Read and write permissions'. The installer" \
               "is still attached to this run as an artifact."
````

## `.github/workflows/jarvis-client.yml`

````yaml
name: Jarvis client

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    paths:
      - "jarvis-client/**"
      # The shared debug key this module is now signed with.
      - "keystore/**"
      - ".github/workflows/jarvis-client.yml"
      # The phone's unit tests also read these (the backend's modules and
      # patches, the desktop's pages and Rust, and the shared test cases in
      # jarvis-desktop/tests/fixtures), so a change there can break them.
      - "backend/**"
      - "jarvis-desktop/src/**"
      - "jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/**"
      - "jarvis-desktop/tests/fixtures/**"
      # The one version number both apps and the backend share.
      - "VERSION"

# Read only by default. Only the `smoke` job, which publishes the APK after
# it has passed, gets write access.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: jarvis-client-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    outputs:
      # The SHA-256 of the certificate in the project key (see "Check the
      # release APK is signed with the project key").
      key_sha256: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.sha256 }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: jarvis-client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - name: Put the signing key back
        # From the DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64 repository secret, not from the repo. The
        # key used to be committed; it was public, so it was removed and
        # replaced. build.gradle.kts still reads keystore/debug.keystore from
        # the repository root, so that is where this writes it.
        #
        # github.workspace is explicit because jarvis-client.yml sets a
        # job-level working-directory of jarvis-client, and this file does not
        # belong there.
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        env:
          KEY: ${{ secrets.DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::The DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64 secret is missing. Stopping on purpose:"
            echo "::error::build.gradle.kts guards the keystore on exists(), so the build"
            echo "::error::would NOT fail - it would sign with a throwaway key, and"
            echo "::error::adb install -r over the copy on the phone would then fail with"
            echo "::error::INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, forcing an uninstall that"
            echo "::error::wipes the pairing secret."
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p keystore
          printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64 -d > keystore/debug.keystore
          echo "Signing key restored."


      - uses: actions/setup-java@dded0888837ed1f317902acf8a20df0ad188d165 # v5.0.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"
          cache: gradle

      - uses: android-actions/setup-android@be39fa834029ff78f1a44aa3bb0819b8fc2bd8fd # v4.0.4
        with:
          # Not the default `tools platform-tools`. Google removed the obsolete
          # `tools` package from the SDK repository, so the action's own default
          # makes it run `sdkmanager tools`, get "Failed to find package 'tools'",
          # and fail the job before a line of this project is compiled. Nothing
          # here ever used it; platform-tools is the half that is real.
          packages: platform-tools

      # The client had no test step at all. It now has tests, and the same
      # results-directory assertion as the other workflow, so "no test sources"
      # cannot pass for green.
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          set -o pipefail
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          if ! ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --stacktrace 2>&1 | tee test.log; then
            echo "::group::Kotlin errors"
            grep -E "^e: |Unresolved reference|Argument type mismatch|None of the following candidates|Compilation error" test.log | head -80 \
              || echo "(none - so this is a TEST failure, not a compile failure)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            # Which tests failed, and why. Gradle prints the assertion above a
            # hundred lines of its own stack trace, so a failing test used to
            # read as "no compiler diagnostics found" and nothing else - the
            # names were in the log and effectively unfindable.
            echo "::group::Failing tests"
            grep -E "FAILED$|^[A-Za-z].*> .* FAILED" test.log | head -40 || true
            results=app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest
            for f in "$results"/TEST-*.xml; do
              [ -e "$f" ] || continue
              python3 - "$f" <<'PYEOF' || true
          import sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
          try:
              root = ET.parse(sys.argv[1]).getroot()
          except Exception:
              sys.exit(0)
          for case in root.iter("testcase"):
              for bad in list(case.findall("failure")) + list(case.findall("error")):
                  print(f'  {case.get("classname")}.{case.get("name")}')
                  # Up to 25 lines, not one. An assertion that lists WHICH
                  # cases disagreed puts the count on line one and the cases
                  # underneath, so printing `msg[0]` reported "8 of 113
                  # vectors" and threw away all eight. The smoke job has
                  # printed 25 since it was written; this half never caught up.
                  # `message` FIRST, not `text`. The attribute is the
                  # assertion alone; the element body is the assertion plus
                  # the whole stack trace. Preferring `text` meant an
                  # assertion that lists eight cases printed one line of
                  # message, eight lines of detail, and then sixteen frames of
                  # JUnit reflection - and the log tail cut the top off, so
                  # the eight were lost a second time by the fix meant to
                  # surface them. Frames are the one thing never in doubt.
                  body = (bad.get("message") or bad.text or "").strip()
                  if not body:
                      body = bad.get("type", "failed")
                  for line in body.splitlines()[:25]:
                      print(f'      {line[:300]}')
          PYEOF
            done
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi
          results=app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest
          if ! ls "$results"/TEST-*.xml >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::No test results in $results — the test task matched no sources."
            exit 1
          fi
          total=$(grep -ho 'tests="[0-9]*"' "$results"/TEST-*.xml \
                  | grep -o '[0-9]*' | paste -sd+ - | bc)
          echo "Total tests: ${total:-0}"
          if [ "${total:-0}" -lt 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::Test results contain zero tests."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Upload test reports
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6.0.0
        with:
          name: jarvis-client-test-reports
          path: jarvis-client/app/build/reports/tests/**
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Assemble debug APK
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          set -o pipefail
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          if ! ./gradlew assembleDebug --stacktrace 2>&1 | tee build.log; then
            echo "::group::Kotlin errors"
            grep -E "^e: |^w: .*error|Unresolved reference|Compilation error" build.log | head -80 \
              || echo "(no compiler diagnostics found; see the full log above)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi

      # No debug APK is uploaded any more (security audit L3). It was
      # debuggable AND signed with the project key, and every build had the
      # same versionCode - so anyone with adb on the unlocked phone could
      # install it over the release, keep the app's data, and use
      # `adb shell run-as` to act as the app and have the Keystore decrypt the
      # pairing token. The release APK below is the one artifact now.
      #
      # THE build that gets published. It is built here, and only here,
      # because this is the one job that has the signing key: the smoke job
      # below downloads this exact file, starts it on an emulator, and
      # publishes it. It never rebuilds it.
      #
      # It used to rebuild it. The smoke job ran its own `assembleRelease` on
      # a fresh machine with no key restored, the Android build tools quietly
      # made a throwaway key there, and every release from 19 Sep 2026 to
      # this fix was published with a different throwaway certificate - so
      # none of them would install over the one before (security audit H1).
      # build.gradle.kts now refuses a release build in CI without the key,
      # and the step after this one compares the certificate itself.
      #
      # R8 breaks at RUNTIME, not at build time - a stripped serializer is a
      # crash on first decode and a green `assembleRelease` - which is why the
      # publish still waits for the smoke job to start this APK on a device.
      - name: Assemble release APK
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          set -o pipefail
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          if ! ./gradlew assembleRelease --stacktrace 2>&1 | tee release.log; then
            echo "::group::Why R8 refused"
            # R8's own complaints, which are not Kotlin diagnostics and do not
            # look like them. A missing keep rule shows up here as a warning
            # about a class it could not find a reference for.
            grep -E "^e: |Missing class|R8: |Warning: |Error: |ProGuard" release.log | head -60               || echo "(nothing that looks like an R8 complaint; see the full log above)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::group::Size"
          debug=$(find app/build/outputs/apk/debug -name '*.apk' | head -1)
          rel=$(find app/build/outputs/apk/release -name '*.apk' | head -1)
          for f in "$debug" "$rel"; do
            [ -n "$f" ] && [ -e "$f" ] && printf '%10s  %s\n' "$(du -h "$f" | cut -f1)" "$f"
          done
          echo "::endgroup::"

      # The certificate inside the APK, compared with the certificate in the
      # key CI restored above. If they differ, the APK was signed with
      # something else (a throwaway key the build tools made, say) and must
      # not be published: the phone would refuse to install it over the copy
      # it has, and the only way past that is an uninstall that wipes the
      # pairing. The fingerprint is handed to the smoke job, which checks the
      # downloaded file against it again right before publishing.
      #
      # A certificate fingerprint is public - it is printed from the APK by
      # anyone who downloads it - so passing it between jobs leaks nothing.
      - name: Check the release APK is signed with the project key
        id: signing
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          apk=app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
          ks="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/keystore/debug.keystore"
          if [ ! -e "$apk" ]; then
            echo "::error::$apk is missing, so there is nothing to check."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ ! -e "$ks" ]; then
            echo "::error::$ks is missing. The restore step should have stopped the job already."
            exit 1
          fi
          sdk="${ANDROID_HOME:-${ANDROID_SDK_ROOT:-}}"
          apksigner=$(find "$sdk/build-tools" -name apksigner -type f 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -n 1) || true
          if [ -z "$apksigner" ]; then
            echo "::error::No apksigner under $sdk/build-tools, so the certificate cannot be checked."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Using $apksigner"

          # keytool prints "SHA256: AB:CD:..."; apksigner prints lowercase hex
          # with no colons. Both are reduced to the second form. awk, not
          # head, so nothing upstream is killed by a closed pipe under
          # pipefail.
          want=$(keytool -list -v -keystore "$ks" -storepass android -alias androiddebugkey \
                 | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*SHA256:[[:space:]]*//p' | awk 'NR == 1' \
                 | tr -d ':[:space:]' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')
          certs=$("$apksigner" verify --print-certs "$apk")
          printf '%s\n' "$certs"
          # Older apksigner prints "Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest: ...", newer
          # (build-tools 37) prints "V2 Signer: certificate SHA-256 digest: ...",
          # once per signing scheme. So count DIFFERENT digests, whatever the prefix.
          digests=$(printf '%s\n' "$certs" \
                | sed -n 's/^.*[Ss]igner.*certificate SHA-256 digest:[[:space:]]*//p' \
                | tr -d ' \t\r' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f' | grep . | sort -u) || true
          signers=$(printf '%s\n' "$digests" | grep -c .) || true
          got=$(printf '%s\n' "$digests" | awk 'NR == 1')

          echo "Key CI restored: ${want:-?}"
          echo "APK is signed:   ${got:-?}"
          if [ "${#want}" -ne 64 ]; then
            echo "::error::Could not read a SHA-256 fingerprint from the restored keystore."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$signers" != "1" ]; then
            echo "::error::Expected exactly one signer in the APK, found ${signers:-0}."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
            echo "::error::The release APK is NOT signed with the project key. Not publishing it."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "sha256=$want" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "The release APK is signed with the project key."

      # Kept 30 days. It is what the smoke job installs and publishes, and it
      # is the fallback if publishing to the release fails. Not debuggable.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6.0.0
        with:
          name: jarvis-client-release-apk
          path: jarvis-client/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

  # The gap that let a crash in onCreate ship with a green tick on every
  # check: the job above compiles the APK and runs unit tests, and never once
  # launches it. This one does, on a real Android image — and because an APK
  # that cannot start is not a release, publishing moved here behind it.
  #
  # No third-party emulator action, deliberately. Every action in this file is
  # pinned to a SHA so it cannot be swapped underneath us, and the one I
  # reached for could not have its SHA verified from where this was written —
  # so it is thirty lines of shell against the SDK that the already-pinned
  # setup-android installs.
  #
  # The APK this job starts and publishes is DOWNLOADED from the build job,
  # not rebuilt here. This job has no signing key, and a rebuild here is
  # exactly how every release from 19 Sep 2026 until this fix went out
  # signed with a throwaway key (security audit H1). download-artifact is
  # pinned below to the commit its v7.0.0 tag pointed at on 2026-09-26 (read
  # from the tag list of github.com/actions/download-artifact).
  #
  # The one job that may write: it publishes the client-latest release.
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build
    timeout-minutes: 35
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # Pinned explicitly because the default is not one path but three, tried
      # in order — $ANDROID_AVD_HOME, $ANDROID_SDK_HOME/avd, $HOME/.android/avd
      # — and avdmanager and the emulator resolved it differently between
      # steps, so a created AVD was simply not there a minute later.
      ANDROID_AVD_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/.avd
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: jarvis-client
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@dded0888837ed1f317902acf8a20df0ad188d165 # v5.0.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"
          cache: gradle

      - uses: android-actions/setup-android@be39fa834029ff78f1a44aa3bb0819b8fc2bd8fd # v4.0.4
        with:
          # Not the default `tools platform-tools`. Google removed the obsolete
          # `tools` package from the SDK repository, so the action's own default
          # makes it run `sdkmanager tools`, get "Failed to find package 'tools'",
          # and fail the job before a line of this project is compiled. Nothing
          # here ever used it; platform-tools is the half that is real.
          packages: platform-tools

      # Without this the emulator drops to pure software emulation and takes
      # long enough to boot that the wait below times out.
      - name: Let the runner use KVM
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' \
            | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm

      - name: Install the system image
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          yes | sdkmanager --licenses >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          sdkmanager --install "system-images;android-34;default;x86_64" \
                               "platforms;android-34" "platform-tools" "emulator"
          # "minutes" versus "tens of minutes" is exactly the difference
          # between having this and not, and it is worth seeing before a
          # timeout rather than after one.
          ls -l /dev/kvm 2>&1 || echo "::warning::/dev/kvm is absent - the emulator will be very slow"

      # Compiled before the device is needed, so a Kotlin error still fails in
      # about a minute rather than after a boot.
      #
      # NOT `assembleRelease`. The release APK comes from the build job (the
      # step after this one), signed with the project key. The debug builds
      # made here are only for the instrumentation tests on the emulator and
      # are never published or uploaded; they are signed with whatever key
      # this machine has, which does not matter for a throwaway emulator.
      - name: Compile the app and the test
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          if ! ./gradlew assembleDebug assembleDebugAndroidTest --stacktrace 2>&1 | tee build.log; then
            echo "::group::Kotlin errors"
            grep -E "^e: |Unresolved reference|Argument type mismatch|Compilation error" build.log | head -80 \
              || echo "(no compiler diagnostics found; see the full log above)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi

      # The one signed release build, made by the build job. Lands at
      # jarvis-client/signed/app-release.apk.
      - name: Fetch the signed release APK from the build job
        uses: actions/download-artifact@37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131 # v7.0.0
        with:
          name: jarvis-client-release-apk
          path: jarvis-client/signed

      # Create, start, wait and test in ONE step. Everything this job has got
      # wrong so far has been state that did not survive a step boundary: the
      # emulator died with the process group that launched it, and then the AVD
      # itself was not where the next step looked for it. Nothing crosses a
      # boundary now except the installed SDK, which is on disk.
      - name: Start the emulator and launch the app
        run: |
          # `-e` is NOT set here, and is on anyway: GitHub runs every `run:`
          # block as `bash -e {0}`. That matters more than it looks. With `-e`
          # and `pipefail` both on, ANY command substitution whose pipeline
          # ends non-zero kills the step on the spot - including a `x=$(...)`
          # assignment written as a question rather than as an action. That is
          # what silently killed this step for three merges; see the pid check
          # at the bottom.
          set -uo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$ANDROID_AVD_HOME"
          if ! echo no | avdmanager create avd -n smoke \
            -k "system-images;android-34;default;x86_64" --force; then
            echo "::error::The AVD could not be created, so there is no device to test on."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Guest Vulkan off, before the emulator is launched.
          #
          # The emulator draws for the guest through a host component called
          # gfxstream, and "Failed to find ColorBuffer: <n>" - which the
          # emulator log tail has carried on every failed run of this job - is
          # gfxstream being handed a handle for a graphics buffer it no longer
          # has. Leaving Vulkan available to the guest gives it a second way to
          # allocate those buffers, and turning it off is the standard
          # workaround for this error on a runner with no GPU. Nothing in this
          # app uses Vulkan - Compose and the GLES faces both go through
          # OpenGL - so there is nothing here for it to take away.
          #
          # This file is an override layer on top of the SDK's own
          # emulator/lib/advancedFeatures.ini, so naming two features leaves
          # every other default alone. It is read from $HOME/.android;
          # ANDROID_AVD_HOME above moves the AVDs, not this.
          #
          # BEST-EFFORT. I cannot run an emulator here to confirm it, and the
          # evidence below says the graphics stack is probably not what is
          # failing anyway. It is cheap, it is documented, and it narrows what
          # the next run has to explain.
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.android"
          printf 'Vulkan = off\nGLDirectMem = on\n' >> "$HOME/.android/advancedFeatures.ini"
          echo "Emulator feature overrides:"; cat "$HOME/.android/advancedFeatures.ini"

          # Assert it exists HERE, so a creation that silently went elsewhere
          # fails on the line that created it rather than five minutes later
          # inside the emulator's own error message.
          if ! "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -list-avds | grep -qx smoke; then
            echo "::error::The AVD was created but the emulator cannot see it."
            echo "ANDROID_AVD_HOME=$ANDROID_AVD_HOME"; ls -la "$ANDROID_AVD_HOME" || true
            "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -list-avds || true
            exit 1
          fi

          # `-gpu swangle_indirect` - ANGLE on SwiftShader's Vulkan - and NOT
          # the old swiftshader_indirect, on evidence. From a4c5ba9 (the
          # Reactor Kit faces) on, five runs in a row lost the emulator
          # process itself during FaceRenderTest; with the face logging each
          # id, both attempts of a run died while Orbit was on screen. A
          # probe then ran FaceRenderTest alone under three modes side by
          # side (run 35907341828): swiftshader_indirect and guest both died
          # on Orbit after 2 faces; swangle_indirect drew all 20, emulator
          # still alive. So the crash lives in the emulator's SwiftShader
          # GLES translator, not in anything this app can see - the app got
          # no error, the host process segfaulted. Guest Vulkan stays off
          # below; this is the HOST's Vulkan, which ANGLE translates to.
          #
          # -memory 4096, up from 2048. A GitHub ubuntu-latest runner has 16GB,
          # and a 2GB Android device that has just finished running a whole
          # instrumentation suite can have Android's low-memory killer take
          # the next app that starts - which looks EXACTLY like the failure
          # here (process gone, nothing in the crash buffer, because a
          # low-memory kill is not a crash and writes nothing there). A guess,
          # but a free one: the exit-info dump added below will say
          # outright if that is what happened.
          start_emulator() {
            "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -avd smoke \
              -no-window -no-audio -no-boot-anim -no-snapshot -no-metrics \
              -camera-back none -camera-front none -memory 4096 \
              -gpu swangle_indirect -accel auto >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/emulator.log" 2>&1 &
            EMU=$!
            if ! timeout 300 adb wait-for-device; then
              echo "::error::The emulator never registered with adb."
              exit 1
            fi
            if ! timeout 600 adb shell 'while [ "$(getprop sys.boot_completed)" != "1" ]; do sleep 2; done'; then
              echo "::error::The emulator registered but never finished booting."
              exit 1
            fi
            adb shell input keyevent 82 || true
            adb devices

            # The device's log, streamed to the RUNNER while the tests run,
            # not read back from the device afterwards. The run for a4c5ba9
            # lost the emulator itself (the host process segfaulted 84s into
            # the suite), and a log that lives on a dead device cannot be
            # read. This copy survives it, and AndroidJUnitRunner's
            # "TestRunner( pid): started:" lines in it name the test that was
            # running when the device went away.
            adb logcat -v time >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/device.log" 2>/dev/null &
            LOGCAT=$!
          }

          finish() {
            # Twelve lines, not a hundred and twenty. This runs on EXIT, so it
            # prints AFTER the failing test names - and GitHub's log API serves
            # a tail, so 120 lines of emulator boot properties pushed the one
            # useful thing out of every window I could fetch. Four log pulls
            # across two runs said only "a test failed" because of this trap.
            #
            # The emulator's own failures are at the end of its log anyway
            # (boot completed, panics, driver errors); the boot-property dump
            # that made up the bulk of it has never once been the answer.

            echo "::group::Emulator log (tail)"
            tail -12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/emulator.log" 2>/dev/null || echo "(none)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            kill "${LOGCAT:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
            kill "${EMU:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
          }
          trap finish EXIT

          # FaceShotTest does NOT run here; it has its own job, `face-shots`,
          # below. The pictures are evidence, not a gate, and a test that can
          # take the whole device down with it must not be what stops the APK
          # being published.
          #
          # ONE fresh emulator if - and only if - the EMULATOR PROCESS died.
          # Three runs in a row (a4c5ba9, 9473ca7, eab1b9c) lost the emulator
          # itself: a segfault in the host process, "Failed to find
          # ColorBuffer" from its software graphics layer, at a different
          # point each time - once in FaceShotTest, once six seconds into
          # FaceRenderTest on the very first face, a face the run before had
          # drawn without trouble. Every run before the Reactor Kit faces
          # (which draw several times more per frame) passed. What that points
          # at is the emulator's software GPU falling over under load, which a
          # phone's real GPU does not share - but it is an inference, not a
          # proof, so it is not hidden: the retry is announced as a warning,
          # a second death fails the job, and a TEST that fails with the
          # emulator still alive is never retried at all.
          # "Gone" is dead OR frozen: in the eab1b9c face-shots job the
          # emulator process stayed alive but adb reported it "offline", and
          # Gradle waited on it for 26 minutes. `timeout` bounds the suite so
          # a frozen device ends the attempt instead of the job.
          emulator_gone() {
            ! kill -0 "$EMU" 2>/dev/null \
              || [ "$(timeout 10 adb get-state 2>/dev/null)" != "device" ]
          }
          run_suite() {
            timeout 900 ./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest --stacktrace \
              -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.notClass=com.jarvis.client.FaceShotTest \
              2>&1 | tee smoke.log
          }
          start_emulator
          suite_ok=1
          run_suite || suite_ok=0
          if [ "$suite_ok" = 0 ] && emulator_gone; then
            echo "::warning::The EMULATOR died or froze during the tests (not the app, not an assertion). Starting a fresh one and running the suite ONE more time."
            kill -9 "$EMU" 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "::group::Emulator log before the retry (last 20 lines)"
            tail -20 "$RUNNER_TEMP/emulator.log" 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "::endgroup::"
            echo "::group::The last tests the device started before it died"
            grep -E "TestRunner\(.*\): (started|finished|failed):" "$RUNNER_TEMP/device.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -4 || true
            echo "::endgroup::"
            kill "$LOGCAT" 2>/dev/null || true
            timeout 30 adb kill-server >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            # A crashed emulator leaves its AVD's lock files behind, and the
            # next one refuses to start on a "running" AVD without this.
            rm -rf "$ANDROID_AVD_HOME"/smoke.avd/*.lock
            start_emulator
            suite_ok=1
            run_suite || suite_ok=0
          fi
          if [ "$suite_ok" = 0 ]; then
            kill "$LOGCAT" 2>/dev/null || true
            # Ordered noisiest-first, so the thing worth reading is LAST.
            # GitHub's log API serves a tail, and the emulator prints ~110
            # lines of boot properties on its way out - enough to push the
            # failing test names out of every window I could fetch. Three
            # separate log pulls said only "a test failed" because of it.
            #
            # Every adb call here has a `timeout`. Without one, `adb logcat`
````
